Subject: Finova: Performance SLOs & regional routing - follow-up

Hi Stephanie / James -

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap so we're aligned and to capture the next steps we agreed on:

What we discussed
- Target SLOs: you mentioned wanting p95 generation latency targets per region and token-length profiles.
- Concurrency / throughput: initial target ~200 concurrent active sessions per region with spikes to 500 for peak batch jobs.
- Streaming: need server-side streaming for UI token-by-token updates; tail-latency expectations ~1-2s to finish streams for short responses.
- Regional routing & data residency: EU customer data must remain in EU (KMS + residency requirement). APAC is a lower-volume region but needs sub-300ms latency targets for Singapore/HK customers.
- Hosting preference: exploring Hosted API for quick POC vs Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput + data controls.

Attachments: I've attached a short Redwood perf summary and a draft MPA we'll iterate on. Also attaching a preliminary SLO matrix that Rishi will flesh out.

Immediate next steps
1) Rishi to map workload characteristics (avg token length, model family, expected QPS per route) and propose an SLO/architecture matrix - target by Friday.
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive (30-45m) with your infra team to validate data residency/KMS needs and routing rules - propose Wed/Thu next week.
3) Share a simple load-test plan and expected throughput numbers for a POC (we can run small-scale perf tests once we have model selection).

If I missed anything, flag it here. Otherwise I'll queue Rishi to start the SLO matrix and Aditya will share an updated commercial timeline.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Finova: Performance SLOs & regional routing - follow-up

Thanks Marissa - this looks right. A few clarifications from our side that will help Rishi scope the matrix:

- SLO targets (initial ask):
  - Short form text generation (<= 64 tokens): p50 < 120ms, p95 < 300ms per region.
  - Long form (>= 256 tokens): p95 < 900ms per token is acceptable for background jobs; interactive sessions should degrade gracefully.
- Streaming: yes, we need token-streaming (SSE/WebSocket) with <2s end-to-end completion for UI flows. We also expect the ability to cancel mid-stream.
- Concurrency/throughput: baseline ~200 concurrent active sessions/region; peak load testing target = 1,500 requests/min across regions (more load will be batched).
- Regional routing/data residency: EU-origin customer data must not leave EU; we have customer-owned KMS (will need to integrate or accept attested HSM). APAC: prefer local routing in Singapore/Hong Kong; if not available we can accept a slightly higher tail latency but prefer sub-300ms.
- Model choices: we plan to test two model families (open-llama-v2 and gptc-lite). Please provide perf numbers for both if you can.

We're happy to do a 30-45m technical call next week - Wed (05/20) morning PT works for our infra lead.

Thanks,
Stephanie Lopez
Head of Platform Engineering | Finova
stephanie.lopez@finova.com

Subject: Re: Finova: Performance SLOs & regional routing - internal recommendation

Folks -

Draft recommendations based on Stephanie's clarifications and our recent perf profiles:

1) Architecture suggestion
- EU: Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) in an EU region with customer KMS integration to meet residency + KMS control.
- US / APAC: Start with Hosted endpoints in-region (US-west, APAC-SG) for fast POC; move to Dedicated if predictable load/throughput demands require it.

2) Streaming and tail-latency
- Use server-side streaming (SSE) with connection-level flow control. For interactive short responses we can hit ~p95 180-300ms on modern A100/T4-like backends with quantized execution paths; long responses will be subject to per-token compute. We should log tail latencies and circuit-break for degraded nodes.

3) Throughput / batching / concurrency
- Propose automatic micro-batching for background/long-run jobs and low-latency continuous batching for interactive sessions. With batching and prefix caching we can support the 200 concurrent sessions target per region on a modest Dedicated pool (suggest 4-8 GPU nodes for initial commit, adjustable after perf run).

4) SLO mapping and tests
- I started the SLO matrix (attached: slo-latency-matrix.xlsx) - need Finova to confirm:
  - Typical prompt lengths (tokens): short (<=64), medium (65-255), long (>=256)
  - % streaming vs request/response flows
  - Model family to test first (open-llama-v2 vs gptc-lite)

5) Data residency / KMS notes
- For EU Dedicated we'll run in-customer VPC or isolated tenancy. For hosted options we can offer attested HSM/KMS integrations but need to verify contractual controls.

Next asks from me: token length distributions and a contact on the Finova infra/KMS side so we can validate the key exchange and attestation flow. I'll prepare a short perf run plan (script + expected QPS) and send it before the technical deep-dive.

Cheers,
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
